text.en: Meena looked at a photo and its enlarged print. "The shape is the same, only bigger," she said.

Similar figures have the same shape but not always the same size. The Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales) says a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio. Its converse is also true, and the angle bisector theorem divides the opposite side in the ratio of the other two sides.
Triangles are similar by the AA, SSS and SAS criteria. The ratio of the areas of similar triangles equals the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides. The Pythagoras theorem and its converse are proved with similar triangles.
A tangent touches a circle at one point and is perpendicular to the radius there. Two tangents drawn from an outside point are equal in length, and the tangent-chord and alternate segment theorems follow. Constructions of tangents and of triangles with given conditions use a ruler and a compass.

problem.en: In a right triangle the legs are 3 and 4. Find the hypotenuse.

prompt.en: A friend says Similar triangles always have equal areas. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: They have the same shape, not always the same size.
Area ratio is the square of the side ratio.

points.en: Thales: a parallel line divides sides proportionally.
Tangents from a point are equal.
Tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
